mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST YoY < -10% in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with rising average hourly earnings (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly), signals a tight labor market with wage inflation, which erodes corporate margins and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth > 0.3% in last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a global supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of 0.75 percentage points or more signals aggressive tightening, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change <= -0.75pp (i.e., increase of 0.75pp or more)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 8% combined with a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (GDPC1 growth < 0%) signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces near-term consumer spending and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during a fiscal stimulus period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate rise above 6.5% during a period when payroll employment (PAYEMS) is also falling signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months, with no concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 5%, signals a supply-side shock rather than demand weakness, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 6 consecutive months AND UNRATE <= 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not significant during a global demand collapse.
